claim: Congenital heart disease affects about 0.5–2.0% of the general population.
source: Congenital heart disease is the most common birth defects and affects about 0.5–2.0% of the general population (Tsao et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tsao et al., 2022

claim: Congenital heart valve defects account for over 25% of all congenital heart disease.
source: Congenital heart valve defects accounts for over 25% of all congenital heart disease (Gilboa et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gilboa et al., 2016

claim: Congenital heart valve defects can be immediately life threatening at birth or impair long-term cardiac function in adulthood.
source: They can be immediately life threatening at birth or impair the long-term cardiac function in adulthood (Zimmerman et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zimmerman et al., 2020

claim: Heart valve development starts with endothelial-mesenchymal-transition (EMT).
source: Heart valve development starts with endothelial-mesenchymal-transition (EMT), in which valvular endothelial cells (VEC) gain mesenchymal markers and invade into the subendothelial matrix to form endocardial cushions.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about heart valve development

claim: During EMT, valvular endothelial cells gain mesenchymal markers and invade into the subendothelial matrix to form endocardial cushions.
source: Heart valve development starts with endothelial-mesenchymal-transition (EMT), in which valvular endothelial cells (VEC) gain mesenchymal markers and invade into the subendothelial matrix to form endocardial cushions.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about EMT process

claim: Post-EMT cells proliferate and differentiate into extracellular matrix producing valvular interstitial cells.
source: Post-EMT, these cells proliferate and differentiate into extracellular matrix (ECM) producing valvular interstitial cells (VIC).
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about post-EMT development

claim: Cellularized endocardial cushions undergo ECM remodeling and elongate into thin mature leaflets or cusps with precise regulation of VEC and VIC.
source: With precise regulation of VEC and VIC, the cellularized endocardial cushions undergo ECM remodeling and elongate into thin mature leaflets or cusps.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about valve maturation

claim: Disturbed growth and remodeling during valve development results in valve malformation and causes clinically relevant cardiac defects.
source: During this process, disturbed growth and remodeling will result in valve malformation and cause clinically relevant cardiac defects (Wu et al., 2017; Gould et al., 2016; Lindsey et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wu et al., 2017; Gould et al., 2016; Lindsey et al., 2015

claim: Genetic causes of valve malformation can explain less than 20% of clinical cases.
source: Genetic causes of this disturbance have been extensively studied, (Yu et al., 2019; MacGrogan et al., 2018; Sifrim et al., 2016) but can explain less than 20% of clinical cases (Pierpont et al., 2018; Gelb and Chung, 2014; Bruneau, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Pierpont et al., 2018; Gelb and Chung, 2014; Bruneau, 2008

claim: The importance of mechanical forces in regulating valve development has become well appreciated.
source: The importance of mechanical forces in regulating valve development has become well appreciated (Chow et al., 2022; Ahuja et al., 2020; Daems et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chow et al., 2022; Ahuja et al., 2020; Daems et al., 2020

claim: Oscillatory shear stress promotes EMT.
source: Oscillatory shear stress (OSS) promotes EMT, and its cellular and molecular mechanisms have been well understood (O'Donnell and Yutzey, 2020a).
evidence: Supported by citation to O'Donnell and Yutzey, 2020a

claim: The role of mechanical forces in post-EMT growth and remodeling remains poorly understood.
source: By contrast, the role of mechanical forces in clinically important post-EMT growth and remodeling remain poorly understood.
evidence: Statement of knowledge gap in the field

claim: Flowing blood generates shear and hydrostatic stress on valves.
source: The flowing blood generates shear and hydrostatic stress on valves.
evidence: Established knowledge about hemodynamic forces

claim: Shear stress is in direct contact with VECs.
source: The shear stress is in direct contact with VECs, while the hydrostatic stress causes compression and tension in valves and can be transmitted to VICs.
evidence: Established knowledge about mechanical force transmission

claim: Hydrostatic stress causes compression and tension in valves and can be transmitted to VICs.
source: The shear stress is in direct contact with VECs, while the hydrostatic stress causes compression and tension in valves and can be transmitted to VICs.
evidence: Established knowledge about mechanical force transmission

claim: Multiple mechanosensitive signaling pathways have been identified in adult tissues.
source: Multiple mechanosensitive signaling pathways have been identified in adult tissues, (De Belly et al., 2022; Souilhol et al., 2020; Vining and Mooney, 2017) but their involvement in valve morphogenesis is unclear.
evidence: Supported by citations to De Belly et al., 2022; Souilhol et al., 2020; Vining and Mooney, 2017

claim: The involvement of mechanosensitive signaling pathways in valve morphogenesis is unclear.
source: Multiple mechanosensitive signaling pathways have been identified in adult tissues, (De Belly et al., 2022; Souilhol et al., 2020; Vining and Mooney, 2017) but their involvement in valve morphogenesis is unclear.
evidence: Statement of knowledge gap

claim: Shear stress regulates early valvulogenesis (EndMT) via bioelectric signaling in zebrafish.
source: Although it has been shown in zebrafish that shear stress regulates early valvulogenesis (namely EndMT) via bioelectric signaling, (Fukui et al., 2021) the near universal VEC in zebrafish heart valves limits study of these later growth and remodeling phases (O'Donnell and Yutzey, 2020b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Fukui et al., 2021

claim: The near universal VEC in zebrafish heart valves limits study of later growth and remodeling phases.
source: Although it has been shown in zebrafish that shear stress regulates early valvulogenesis (namely EndMT) via bioelectric signaling, (Fukui et al., 2021) the near universal VEC in zebrafish heart valves limits study of these later growth and remodeling phases (O'Donnell and Yutzey, 2020b).
evidence: Supported by citation to O'Donnell and Yutzey, 2020b

claim: The contributions of VICs and hydrostatic stress in valvulogenesis are not known.
source: The contributions of VICs and hydrostatic stress, including potential collaborations with VEC, in valvulogenesis are not known.
evidence: Statement of knowledge gap

claim: YAP signaling is a widely investigated mechanoactive pathway.
source: YAP signaling is another widely investigated mechanoactive pathway, (Dupont et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2016) and transcriptional cofactor of the Hippo pathway (Moya and Halder, 2019).

claim: YAP is a transcriptional cofactor of the Hippo pathway.
source: YAP signaling is another widely investigated mechanoactive pathway, (Dupont et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2016) and transcriptional cofactor of the Hippo pathway (Moya and Halder, 2019).

claim: YAP signaling regulates cardiac ventricular development by promoting cardiomyocyte proliferation.

claim: The role of YAP in post-EndMT valvular morphogenesis is poorly understood.
source: However, its role in post-EndMT valvular morphogenesis is poorly understood.

claim: YAP was expressed in both mesenchyme and endothelium of outflow tract and atrioventricular cushions at E11.5.

claim: Cytoplasmic YAP expression in VECs on the inflow side was stronger throughout all stages.

claim: YAP activity in chick embryonic hearts followed the same spatiotemporal pattern as in mouse hearts.

claim: YAP activation in VICs surged at HH30 then dropped at HH36 in chick embryonic hearts.

claim: VECs on the outflow side had an upregulated nuclear YAP expression in chick embryonic hearts.
source: VECs on the outflow side had an upregulated nuclear YAP expression while YAP expression in VECs on the inflow side was mainly in cytoplasm.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: YAP expression in VECs on the inflow side was mainly in cytoplasm in chick embryonic hearts.
source: VECs on the outflow side had an upregulated nuclear YAP expression while YAP expression in VECs on the inflow side was mainly in cytoplasm.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: YAP target genes THBS1, ANKRD1 and PTX3 were elevated by almost 10-fold at E14.5 compared to E11.5 cushions.
source: YAP target genes THBS1, ANKRD1 and PTX3 were elevated by almost 10-fold at E14.5 and HH31 when compared to E11.5 or HH25 cushions, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).

claim: YAP target genes THBS1, ANKRD1 and PTX3 were elevated by almost 10-fold at HH31 compared to HH25 cushions.
source: YAP target genes THBS1, ANKRD1 and PTX3 were elevated by almost 10-fold at E14.5 and HH31 when compared to E11.5 or HH25 cushions, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: The expressions of YAP target genes reduced significantly during later stages of remodeling.

claim: Gene expressions of LATS1/2 had little change during valve growth and remodeling.

claim: YAP activity during valve remodeling was largely independent of the Hippo pathway.

claim: The spatiotemporal activation of YAP correlated with changes in the mechanical environment.
source: In addition to the co-effector of the Hippo pathway, YAP is also a key mediator in mechanotransduction. Indeed, the spatiotemporal activation of YAP correlated with the changes in the mechanical environment.

claim: Unidirectional shear stress developed on the inflow surface of valves during valve remodeling.
source: During valve remodeling, unidirectional shear stress (USS) developed on the inflow surface of valves, where YAP was rarely expressed in the nuclei of VECs (Figure 2A).

claim: YAP was rarely expressed in the nuclei of VECs on the inflow surface where unidirectional shear stress developed.
source: During valve remodeling, unidirectional shear stress (USS) developed on the inflow surface of valves, where YAP was rarely expressed in the nuclei of VECs (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Oscillatory shear stress developed on the outflow surface of valves during valve remodeling.
source: On the other side, OSS developed on the outflow surface, where VECs with nuclear YAP localized.
evidence: Established knowledge about hemodynamic patterns and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2A

claim: VECs with nuclear YAP localized on the outflow surface where oscillatory shear stress developed.
source: On the other side, OSS developed on the outflow surface, where VECs with nuclear YAP localized.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2A

claim: YAP activation in VICs correlated with hydrostatic pressure.
source: The YAP activation in VICs also correlated with hydrostatic pressure.
evidence: Inferred from correlation between YAP localization and stress patterns

claim: Compressive stress was generated in the tips of valves where VICs with nuclear YAP localized.
source: The pressure generated compressive stress (CS) in the tips of valves, where VICs with nuclear YAP localized (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B

claim: Tensile stress was created in the elongated regions of valves where YAP was absent in VIC nuclei.
source: Although tensile stress (TS) was created in the elongated regions, where YAP was absent in VIC nuclei.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2B

claim: High unidirectional shear stress restricted YAP in cytoplasm of VECs.
source: The VEC was obtained from AV cushions of chick embryonic hearts at HH25. The cushions were placed on collagen gels with endocardium adherent to the collagen and incubated to enable the VECs to migrate onto the gel. We then removed the cushions and immediately applied the shear flow to the monolayer for 24 hr. The low stress OSS (2 dyn/cm2) promoted YAP nuclear translocation in VEC (Figure 2C and E), while high stress USS (20 dyn/cm2) restrained YAP in cytoplasm.
evidence: Supported by in vitro shear stress experiments shown in Figure 2C and E

claim: Low oscillatory shear stress promoted YAP nuclear translocation in VEC.
source: The low stress OSS (2 dyn/cm2) promoted YAP nuclear translocation in VEC (Figure 2C and E), while high stress USS (20 dyn/cm2) restrained YAP in cytoplasm.
evidence: Supported by in vitro shear stress experiments shown in Figure 2C and E

claim: Compressive stress was induced by hypertonic condition in the cushion explant culture system.
source: To study the effect of hydrostatic stress on the YAP activation in VICs, we used media with different osmolarities to mimic the CS and TS. CS was induced by hypertonic condition while TS was created by hypotonic condition, and the Unloaded (U) condition refers to the osmotically balanced media.
evidence: Description of experimental method

claim: Tensile stress was created by hypotonic condition in the cushion explant culture system.
source: CS was induced by hypertonic condition while TS was created by hypotonic condition, and the Unloaded (U) condition refers to the osmotically balanced media.
evidence: Description of experimental method

claim: Osmotic pressure provides a reliable model to mimic hydrostatic pressure in vitro.
source: Notably, in vivo hydrostatic pressure is generated by flowing blood, while in vivo osmotic pressure is generated by cardiac contractility and plays a critical role in the mechanotransduction during valve development (Vignes et al., 2022). Despite the different in vivo origination, the osmotic pressure provides a reliable model to mimic the hydrostatic pressure in vitro (Bassen et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vignes et al., 2022 and Bassen et al., 2021

claim: Trapezoidal cushions adopted a spherical shape after 24-hour culture.
source: We cultured HH27 AV cushion explants under different loading conditions for 24 hr and found that the trapezoidal cushions adopted a spherical shape (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by morphological data shown in Figure 2D

claim: Tensile stress loaded cushions significantly compacted.
source: TS loaded cushions significantly compacted, and the YAP activation in VICs of TS-loaded cushions was significantly lower than that in CS loaded VICs (Figure 2F).
evidence: Supported by morphological and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2D and 2F

claim: YAP activation in VICs of tensile stress-loaded cushions was significantly lower than that in compressive stress loaded VICs.
source: TS loaded cushions significantly compacted, and the YAP activation in VICs of TS-loaded cushions was significantly lower than that in CS loaded VICs (Figure 2F).
evidence: Supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2F

claim: Verteporfin inhibits the interaction between YAP and TEAD.
source: The VP inhibits the interaction between YAP and TEAD, which in turn, blocks transcriptional activation of targets downstream of YAP (Kagawa et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kagawa et al., 2022

claim: Verteporfin at 5 mM concentration did not compromise cell viability.

claim: YAP inhibition reduced cushion size regardless of media condition.

claim: Valves cultured in media with verteporfin maintained their trapezoidal shape.

claim: Loss of YAP significantly inhibits the proliferation of VIC.

claim: YAP inhibition significantly strengthened the expression of VE-cadherin between VECs.

claim: YAP inhibited valves showed five or more layers of endothelium.

claim: PY-60 treatment promoted the association of YAP and TEAD.

claim: Cell viability did not compromise by PY-60 (10 mM) treatments.
source: Cell viability did not compromise by PY-60 (10 mM) treatments (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by live/dead staining data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B

claim: YAP activation reversed the compaction trend of valves under tensile stress and unloaded conditions.

evidence: Supported by morphological data shown in Figure 4A and 4B

claim: YAP activation drove growth in valve size.
source: YAP activation reversed the compaction trend of valves under TS and U conditions and drove a growth in valve size (Figure 4A vs. Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by morphological data shown in Figure 4A and 4B

claim: All valves adopted spherical shape regardless of whether they grew or compacted.

claim: YAP activation significantly elevated VIC proliferation regardless of loading conditions.

claim: The expression of VE-cadherin in YAP activated endothelium was significantly weaker than that in YAP inhibited endothelium.

claim: YAP inhibition gave a similar stiffness increase to the nearly linear increase in valve stiffness from HH25 to HH34 observed in previous studies.

claim: The stiffness of YAP activated valves was only half of that of YAP inhibited valves.

claim: Left atrial ligation restricted blood flow in the left ventricle.

We collected the hearts during cushion remodeling (HH31) when the valves begin to take shape. The LAL restricted the blood flow in the left ventricle, resulting in a reduced hemodynamic stress and shear stress on left AV valves but augmented forces on the right AV valves.

claim: Left atrial ligation resulted in reduced hemodynamic stress and shear stress on left AV valves.
source: The LAL restricted the blood flow in the left ventricle, resulting in a reduced hemodynamic stress and shear stress on left AV valves but augmented forces on the right AV valves.

claim: Left atrial ligation augmented forces on the right AV valves.
source: The LAL restricted the blood flow in the left ventricle, resulting in a reduced hemodynamic stress and shear stress on left AV valves but augmented forces on the right AV valves.
evidence: Expected mechanical consequence of LAL procedure

claim: LAL valves and hearts had smaller sizes compared with control valves and hearts.

claim: Neural crest cells make a major contribution to the OFT cushions but a minor contribution to AV and intercalated cushions.
source: Cells derived from the second heart field make the major contribution to the OFT walls, and neural crest cells make a major contribution to the OFT cushions but a minor contribution to AV and intercalated cushions (Eley et al., 2018; Henderson et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Eley et al., 2018; Henderson et al., 2020

claim: During post-EMT growth and remodeling, all valves with various morphologies are formed by identical VECs and VICs.
source: However, during the post-EMT growth and remodeling, all valves with various morphologies are formed by identical VECs and VICs.
evidence: Established knowledge about valve cell composition

claim: The collaboration between VECs and VICs, instead of a specific cell lineage, determines valve growth and remodeling.
source: Our study supports that the collaboration between VECs and VICs, instead of a specific cell lineage, determines the valve growth and remodeling.
evidence: Inferred from all experimental results showing mechanical regulation of both cell types

claim: Spatiotemporally coordinated mechanotransduction of shear and hydrostatic stress is required for proper valve growth and remodeling.
source: In conclusion, our study shows that the spatiotemporally coordinated mechanotransduction of shear and hydrostatic stress is required for proper valve growth and remodeling.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from all experimental results

claim: Shear and hydrostatic stress can regulate VEC tensions and VIC proliferation by YAP pathways and thus determine valve size and shape.
source: The shear and hydrostatic stress can regulate VEC tensions and VIC proliferation by YAP pathways and thus determine the valve size and shape.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from all experimental results

claim: Malfunctional YAP signaling could cause valve malformation.
source: Malfunctional YAP signaling could cause valve malformation, but improper local mechanical signaling imposes a more important malformation risk, even if the YAP signaling is fully functional and no genes are mutated.
evidence: Inferred from experimental results showing effects of YAP manipulation

claim: Improper local mechanical signaling imposes a more important malformation risk than malfunctional YAP signaling, even if YAP signaling is fully functional and no genes are mutated.
source: Malfunctional YAP signaling could cause valve malformation, but improper local mechanical signaling imposes a more important malformation risk, even if the YAP signaling is fully functional and no genes are mutated.
evidence: Inferred from LAL experimental results showing malformation despite normal genetic background

claim: The presented mechanobiological system could open an opportunity to control valve growth and change valve shape by influencing forces or targeting YAP pathway at a specific stage.
source: The presented mechanobiological system could also open an opportunity to control valve growth and change valve shape by influencing forces or targeting YAP pathway at a specific stage.
evidence: Speculative statement about potential applications

claim: Four-chambered chick hearts develop in a manner that mirrors human heart development.
source: The four-chambered chick hearts develop in a manner that mirrors human heart development.
evidence: Established knowledge about chick as a model organism

claim: LAL has been shown to replicate some important features of congenital heart defects.
source: The LAL manipulates mechanical forces in vivo and has been shown to replicate some important features of congenital heart defects (Gould et al., 2016; Salman et al., 2021; Ho et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gould et al., 2016; Salman et al., 2021; Ho et al., 2021

claim: Cushion explants tend to form a sphere in a way similar to the clustering of cells to minimize surface tension.
source: In terms of shape, cushion explants tend to form a sphere in a way similar to the clustering of cells to minimize the surface tension (Ninomiya and Winklbauer, 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ninomiya and Winklbauer, 2008 and observed morphological changes

claim: The densely packed endothelium in YAP inhibited valves could be a result of large shrinkage in surface area.
source: The densely packed endothelium could be a result of the large shrinkage in surface area, during which the endothelium at 0 hr could be geometrically too large for the valves at 24 hr.
evidence: Speculative explanation for observed multilayered endothelium

claim: YAP activity can affect cell-cell junctions between VECs.
source: Another possibility is that YAP activity can affect cell-cell junctions between VECs.
evidence: Inferred from VE-cadherin expression data

claim: YAP can break cell-cell junctions via SMADs mediated TGF-β signaling during the EMT process.
source: For example, studies reported that YAP can break cell-cell junctions via SMADs mediated TGF-β signaling during the EMT process (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhang et al., 2014

claim: Simple interactions between mesenchymal and endothelial cells provide basic elements for tissue morphogenesis.
source: In fact, the simple interactions between mesenchymal and endothelial provide basic elements for tissue morphogenesis (Hughes et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hughes et al., 2018

claim: Blood flow initiates an asymmetric deformation of the cushion.
source: The blood flow initiates an asymmetric deformation of the cushion (Figure 6B), leaving a gradient stress distribution with highest stress on the top (Buskohl et al., 2012b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Buskohl et al., 2012b and illustrated in Figure 6B

claim: Blood flow leaves a gradient stress distribution with highest stress on the top of the cushion.
source: The blood flow initiates an asymmetric deformation of the cushion (Figure 6B), leaving a gradient stress distribution with highest stress on the top (Buskohl et al., 2012b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Buskohl et al., 2012b
